title: Bilbao Crystallographic Server: I. Databases and crystallographic computing programs
relevance_reason: The paper is entirely about crystallographic databases (space groups, symmetry data) and group-theoretical computing tools; it does not mention or address vector databases, vector indexing, or nearest-neighbor similarity search in any way.
research_focus: Description of the Bilbao Crystallographic Server, a web-based platform providing crystallographic databases (space groups, subperiodic groups, k-vectors) and group-theoretical computing programs for group-subgroup relations and Wyckoff position splitting.
method: Web-based database system with simple retrieval tools (HTML, ASCII, XML output) and group-theoretical algorithms for computing subgroups, supergroups, conjugacy classes, and Wyckoff-position splitting schemes.
results_summary: The paper reports on the current state of the Bilbao Crystallographic Server after nearly six years of operation, describing its core databases of space-group symmetry data, maximal subgroups, subperiodic groups, and k-vector classifications. It details the retrieval tools that provide access to this data in multiple formats and the crystallographic computing programs that apply group-theoretical algorithms to determine subgroups, supergroups, and Wyckoff-position splitting. The server is presented as an integrated working environment where programs can communicate with each other, using one program's output as another's input. The utility of the applications is demonstrated through illustrative examples. The remaining programs on the server are deferred to a forthcoming article.
research_gaps: The programs related to representations of space groups and point groups, and applications for solid-state physics and structural chemistry, are the subject of a forthcoming article
